title: The bias interval of the elephant random walk
author: Arjun Pemmasani
abstract:
We prove the conjecture of Gu\'erin, Laulin, Raschel and Simon
that the bimodal initial biases of the superdiffusive elephant random walk
form a possibly empty open interval centered at one half. Outside it,
including its endpoints, the limit density has a unique local maximum.
Finite sign bounds pass to the limit under weak convergence.
They give exactly two inflection points for the fair unimodal density
and four for the bimodal density. A moment argument proves bimodality
for memory at least $0.79$ without computation.

A certificate locates the unique fair-start transition
near $0.66881286$. The critical density has a quartic top.
Its two modes separate on a square-root scale, while the bias interval
opens on a three-halves scale. Above the threshold, the bias boundary
is positive and continuously differentiable, with a variational formula
and a unique optimizer. Thus strongly biased starts are unimodal at
every fixed memory, although the boundary tends to zero as memory
tends to one.
